text:
maya: Heads up — ap-southeast cluster saw ~120 pending GPU pods for the past 20m, but nodepools show low GPU allocation. Suspect fractional-GPU packing + autoscaler + IP allocation mismatch. Anyone seen this pattern?

aj: Can you paste the pending pod errors and a node summary? `kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o wide` and `kubectl describe node gpu-timeslice-az1-0001` would help.

maya: Paste of describe (trimmed):
```
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----     ------            ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  5m    default-scheduler  0/8 nodes are available: 8 Insufficient alpha.nvidia.com/gpu, 4 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict.
  Warning  FailedScheduling  4m    kubelet            0/8 nodes are available: 8 max pods per node 110, but CNI allocatable IPs exhausted on some nodes.
```
Also seeing device-plugin advertise fractional allocatable GPUs like "0.25" per pod.

sophia: Sounds like two simultaneous constraints: (1) our fractional GPU packing (we pack 4x 0.25 pods per GPU) but the MIG/time-slice nodepool shapes are misaligned with pod placement, causing fragmentation; (2) CNI/ENI limits in ap-southeast mean nodes report lower max-pods -> autoscaler thinks adding nodes won't help because of pod-IP exhaustion rules.

liam: Correct — ap-southeast subnets were sized conservatively last year. We also use EIPs for outbound NLBs which reduce available primary IPs. That interacts badly with aws-vpc-cni default `WARM_PREFIXES` settings.

aj: Autoscaler config excerpt I checked in staging: 
```
--scale-down-enabled=true
--balance-similar-node-groups
--expander=most-pods
--max-node-provision-time=20m
```
With `most-pods` it prefers nodepools with higher pod packing, but because some nodes advertise lower max-pods the scaler is hesitating.

diego: Workarounds we tried before: bump `--expander=least-waste` so CA prefers filling existing GPUs, and enable CNI prefix delegation / increase ENI quotas. But prefix delegation requires VPC subnet change for ap-southeast.

infra-bot: Patch candidate created by @aj at 1965432201: set autoscaler expander to "least-waste" for gpu-* nodepools and add 2 nodes to gpu-timeslice-az1 in staging.

aj: I pushed a small change to staging: annotated nodes with `gpu.sharing=timeslice`, added taint `gpu.sharing=timeslice:NoSchedule` on gp-timeslice pool so scheduler prefers those nodes for fractional pods, and reduced `--max-node-provision-time` to 15m to be more aggressive.

sophia: Longer-term we should: (a) standardize pod GPU request sizes to match MIG profiles (e.g., 1g vs 0.5g) so fragmentation lowers, (b) enable prefix delegation or enlarge subnets in ap-southeast to avoid IP exhaustion, (c) re-evaluate whether time-slicing is worth it in low-ENI regions.

maya: Short-term decision: scale up gpu-timeslice pool by +4 nodes in ap-southeast and enable prefix delegation alpha flag on the CNI for that cluster to test. I'll open infra ticket for subnet resize and cost impact. :white_check_mark:

liam: Cost FYI — +4 nodes in ap-southeast using our reserved commit is ~ $12k/month; if we keep them on spot it varies a lot. Proposal: 50% reserved commit for that AZ while we stabilize.

maya: Thanks all. I'll monitor pending pods and post updates here. If we still see fragmentation after the CNI change, we'll migrate small-batch workloads to a 1g MIG profile.
